stem.text: The temperature of a liquid in a laboratory flask is modeled by \( H(t) = 60 + 75 e^{- \frac{t}{12}} \) degrees Celsius, for \( 0 \le t \le 36 \), where t is measured in minutes. Using a calculator, find \( H'(3) \), showing the setup, and interpret the value in the context of the problem with correct units. Give the value correct to three decimal places.

answer_key.label: \( H'(3) = -4.868 \), so at time t = 3 minutes the temperature of the liquid is decreasing at a rate of 4.868 degrees Celsius per minute.

worked_solution.text: Differentiate the model to get the rate, \( H'(t) = - \frac{25 e^{- \frac{t}{12}}}{4} \).
With a calculator, \( H'(3) = -4.868 \) to three decimal places.
worked_solution.rule_named: evaluate the derivative at the instant

worked_solution.text: The value is negative, so at time t = 3 minutes the temperature of the liquid is decreasing at a rate of 4.868 degrees Celsius per minute.
worked_solution.rule_named: sign of the rate gives the direction of change
